refnamediv.refpurpose: filter to convert Unifont HEX fonts to YAFF fonts

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: hex2yaff.pl reads a font in Unifont HEX format from its standard input and prints the font in Yet Another Font Format (YAFF) format to its standard output.

Height in the size field is taken from the height given in the HEX file using the vtfontcvt1 convention. The width likewise given in the HEX file determines the number of pixels in each line of the YAFF font (rounding widths up to the next multiple of 4 pixels). The --width and --rows command‐line options provide default width and height information if the HEX font is missing it.

The output of bdf2hex.pl1 will almost always (unless the original BDF font also lacked metadata) have height and width metadata. The HEX fonts built in Unscii have these metadata. All of the HEX fonts used in FreeBSD come with these metadata, also.
refsection.note: Using --width or --rows at this point in a chain of font conversions is usually an indication that size information has been incorrectly thrown away by an earlier tool.
refsection.para: The --copyright, --version, --variant, and --slant command‐line options provide metadata to be placed in the font properties of the BDF file. These metadata are not present in Unifont HEX files.

refsection.title: Bugs
refsection.para: The YAFF format supports arbitrary widths. But the HEX format has an effective granularity of 1 nybble (i.e. one hexadecimal digit) in its pixel data, even though its metadata can specify widths that are not aligned to that. No attempt is made to mask off extra pixels beyond the specified width. Unusually sized HEX fonts will be widened to a multiple of 4 pixels wide, and will include possibly bogus extra pixels that were in the HEX data.
